test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and State governments.
 
• It is enumerated in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• In case of conflict between the Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects of local or state importance like police, public health, agriculture, and fisheries. Only the State Legislatures can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal structure, where powers are divided between the central and state governments, with a strong centralizing bias.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The division of powers between the Union and State governments is outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• **Residual Powers:** Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are vested in the Parliament.
